title: O Source Divine, and Life of All
description: O Source Divine, and Life of All in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Sterling wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 75, “Love Supreme in God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Source di-vine, and Life of all, The Fount of be-ing's won-drous sea! Thy depth would ev-ery heart ap-pall, That saw not Love su-preme in Thee.

lines: O Source divine, and Life of all,
The Fount of being's wondrous sea!
Thy depth would every heart appall,
That saw not Love supreme in Thee.
We shrink before Thy vast abyss,
Where worlds on worlds eternal brood;
We know Thee truly but in this,
That Thou bestowest all our good.
And so, 'mid boundless time and space,
O, grant us still in Thee to dwell,
And through the ceaseless web to trace
Thy presence working all things well!
Nor let Thou life's delightful play
Thy truth's transcendent vision hide;
Nor strength and gladness lead astray
From Thee, our nature's only guide.
Bestow on every joyous thrill
Thy deeper tone of reverent awe;
Make pure Thy children's erring will,
And teach their hearts to love Thy law!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Sterling died in 1844.
credits: Words by John Sterling (1806–1844), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
